## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dutiyasuppaṭicchanna* rule (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 4, "Not being well-covered") is a monastic training rule (*sekhiya*) preserved within the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It governs decorous comportment and monastic attire, specifically mandating that a monk be well covered when sitting down in inhabited areas [SuttaCentral; Stache-Rosen 1984]. In her comparative study of Vinaya texts, Valentina Stache-Rosen observes that the Pali Vibhaṅga to Sekhiya 4 (alongside Sekhiyas 10, 20, and 24) identifies an exemption for a monk who has entered upon a permanent rains residence (*vāsūpagatassa*), in contrast to the parallel rule in the Chinese *Upāliparipṛcchāsūtra*, which excuses non-compliance when the monk is sleeping [Stache-Rosen 1984]. An English translation of the rule and its word commentary has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral show extensive transmission across early Buddhist lineages: within the Pali tradition, it corresponds to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Sekhiya 4, Bhikkhu Parivāra Sekhiya 4, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 4, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Sekhiya 4, and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Sekhiya 4 [SuttaCentral]. Cross-tradition parallels are attested in the Sanskrit Prātimokṣasūtra of the Sarvāstivādins as well as Chinese Vinaya texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and *Upāliparipṛcchā* traditions [SuttaCentral]. According to DharmaNexus, the text exhibits 103 internal Pali text-reuse matches across 47 texts, reflecting substantial structural and phrasal overlap with adjacent Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga *sekhiya* training rules, most notably Sekhiyas 16, 20, 7, 12, 15, and 24 [DharmaNexus].
